content.question: What happens when the button is clicked once?

options.text: `handleClick` is passed to React and then called by React when the click happens.
`handleClick` runs before the page is shown.
React stores the function result as the button text.

feedback.correct: `onClick={handleClick}` passes a function. React calls that function when the user clicks.
feedback.incorrect: `onClick={handleClick}` passes a function. React calls that function when the user clicks.

content.title: The classic mistake
content.text:
Compare these two lines:

```jsx
<button onClick={handleClick}>Save</button>
<button onClick={handleClick()}>Save</button>
```

They are not equivalent.

`onClick={handleClick}` means: “Here is the function to call later.”

`onClick={handleClick()}` means: “Run this function right now and use its return value here.”

content.title: Fix it
Event handlers and state
